rows.note: Fact: the numerical coincidence m_p/m_e ≈ 6 pi^5 was published by F. Lenz, Phys. Rev. 82, 554 (1951); the repo cites Lenz (Prologue, mass-ratio chain page). No continuous input pins the value; the result is set by discrete choices (exponent source via MAP-2, n = 3, S^1 vs S^2 averaging, alpha placement). Alternatives give 6 pi^3 = 186.0, 6 pi^7 = 18122, n=2 -> 124.0, n=4 -> 24162. Per the review, LOCK-NU-N was adopted after 6 pi^5 was known (accommodation, not a continuous fit). Classed anchor-restatement in the sense of selected discrete parameters; look-elsewhere chance in the n*pi^k family (n<=12, k in -6..8) is about 4e-4 (lee_6pi5.py).

rows.claim: Proton radius r_p = D/(6 pi^6) (reclassified from locked input to prediction)
rows.note: r_p was a locked input (0.8412 fm) before reclassification. The '+61 ppm independent cross-check' is the 18.8 ppm residual plus a 42.4 ppm rounding of the old lock (identity).
